title: The Hot, Continuum-compact State of the Yellow Hypergiant V509 Cassiopeiae: CHARA Diameters, CO-band Angular-extension Constraints, and Companion Limits
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal; 6 figures, 4 tables and 15 pages
summary: Yellow hypergiants are rare, evolved massive stars generally interpreted as post-red-supergiant objects evolving blueward through or near the dynamically unstable Yellow Evolutionary Void. V509~Cassiopeiae is a remarkable example: its spectroscopically inferred effective temperature increased from approximately 5000~K in the mid-1980s to about 7900~K by the late 1990s and has since remained near this value during its post-heating state. We use simultaneous six-telescope CHARA observations obtained in 2023 with MIRC-X in the $H$ band and MYSTIC in the $K$ band to measure its photospheric diameter, search for a luminous companion, and constrain any spatially extended CO atmosphere. Interferometric data fitting with fixed atmosphere-model center-to-limb variation profiles yield limb-darkened angular diameters of $1.1840$--$1.1950$~mas. Although nominally about 5\% smaller than the previous Palomar Testbed Interferometer measurement, the difference is only $1.8σ$, indicating no significant secular change over 17--21~yr. The closure phases are consistent with a centrosymmetric brightness distribution, and no near-infrared-bright companion is detected over the sampled separations. The median $3σ$ limits are $ΔH=5.28$~mag and $ΔK=6.48$~mag. The B1~V companion proposed from ultraviolet spectroscopy is expected to lie below these limits and is not excluded. The CO first-overtone channels give a weighted mean CO-to-continuum diameter ratio of $1.011\pm0.004$, below the adopted $3σ$ detection criterion. We find no significant CO-band angular extension. V509~Cas is thus hot and molecularly compact despite retaining spectroscopically visible atomic circumstellar gas.

AI.tldr: The paper reports CHARA array interferometric observations of the yellow hypergiant V509 Cas, measuring its limb-darkened angular diameter (1.184–1.195 mas), finding no significant secular change versus previous measurements, no detected near-infrared companion, and no significant CO-band extension, concluding the star is hot and molecularly compact.
AI.motivation: Yellow hypergiants are rare evolved massive stars thought to be post-red-supergiant objects evolving through the dynamically unstable Yellow Evolutionary Void. V509 Cas is notable for its rapid spectroscopic temperature increase from ~5000 K (mid-1980s) to ~7900 K (late 1990s), and this work aims to measure its current photospheric diameter, search for a luminous companion, and constrain any spatially extended CO atmosphere during its post-heating state.
AI.method: The authors used simultaneous six-telescope CHARA observations from 2023 with MIRC-X (H band) and MYSTIC (K band). They fitted interferometric data with fixed atmosphere-model center-to-limb variation profiles to derive limb-darkened angular diameters, examined closure phases for asymmetry/companion detection, established companion magnitude limits, and analyzed CO first-overtone channel diameters for atmospheric extension.
AI.result: The limb-darkened angular diameter is 1.1840–1.1950 mas, about 5% smaller than the previous Palomar Testbed Interferometer measurement but only a 1.8-sigma difference, indicating no significant secular change over 17–21 yr. Closure phases are consistent with centrosymmetry and no near-infrared-bright companion is detected (median 3-sigma limits of ΔH=5.28 mag and ΔK=6.48 mag). The weighted mean CO-to-continuum diameter ratio is 1.011±0.004, below the 3-sigma detection criterion, so no significant CO-band angular extension is found.
AI.conclusion: V509 Cas is confirmed to be hot and molecularly compact despite retaining spectroscopically visible atomic circumstellar gas. The previously proposed B1 V companion is not excluded by these observations, and the star shows no significant secular diameter change or CO extension.

title: Statistical Energy Budget of the Solar Wind with Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter : 1 - Unbalanced Total Energy Radial Evolution
summary: The magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) description of the solar wind has long been regarded as one of the most successful frameworks for investigating solar wind heating and acceleration. Under a set of simplifying assumptions, it provides a reduced large-scale description that is widely used to study the energetic role of electromagnetic fluctuations in the solar wind energy budget. In practice, applying simplification to MHD can result in the loss of some physics compared to an exact set of equations. However, an observational energy budget can help us to verify whether any energetic information has been lost in the process of simplification. To do so, we directly test the validity of the large-scale non-linear ideal MHD energy budget with solar wind observations from Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter (SO). After verifying the reliability of the measurements through comparison with previous studies of similar solar wind properties, we test the conservation of the total energy predicted by the MHD theory. We find that the average total energy increases with radial distance by $56\%$ ($\pm9\%$) between 14 and 203 solar radii. The increase in kinetic energy is not sufficiently compensated by the decrease of the thermal and electromagnetic contributions. We investigate the major sources of observational uncertainty and find that they cannot account for the observed energy increase. These results suggest that the large-scale theoretical description may neglect an energetically significant contribution to solar wind acceleration. Assuming that such a contribution exists, we predict that this extra energy would scale with radial distance as $r^{-0.54\pm0.38}$.

AI.tldr: The paper tests the validity of the large-scale non-linear ideal MHD energy budget using Parker Solar Probe and Solar Orbiter observations. The authors find that average total energy increases by 56% (±9%) between 14 and 203 solar radii, which cannot be explained by observational uncertainties, suggesting the large-scale MHD description may neglect an energetically significant contribution to solar wind acceleration with a predicted radial scaling of r^-0.54±0.38.
AI.motivation: The large-scale MHD description of the solar wind, while widely used, is subject to simplifying assumptions that may lose physics compared to exact equations. The authors aim to directly verify whether energetic information is lost in the simplification process by using an observational energy budget.
AI.method: The authors directly test the non-linear ideal MHD energy budget against in-situ solar wind observations from Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter (SO). They first verify measurement reliability through comparison with previous studies, then test conservation of total energy predicted by MHD theory, and finally assess sources of observational uncertainty and the radial scaling of any missing energy contribution.
AI.result: The average total energy increases by 56% (±9%) with radial distance between 14 and 203 solar radii. The increase in kinetic energy is not compensated by decreases in thermal and electromagnetic contributions. Observational uncertainties cannot account for the observed energy increase. If an additional energy contribution exists, it would scale as r^-0.54±0.38.
AI.conclusion: The large-scale ideal MHD energy budget is not closed when tested against PSP and SO observations, indicating that an energetically significant contribution to solar wind acceleration may be neglected in the simplified MHD description. This suggests the need for additional physical mechanisms or terms in the theoretical framework.

title: Evolution of Stellar Activity and Habitable Zone (EATEN): III. X-ray Activity of Dwarfs in Open Clusters and Field Stars
comment: 22 pages, 16 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJS
summary: Stellar X-ray emission serves as a direct diagnostic of coronal activity, which is fundamentally linked to coronal heating processes. It also strongly influences the atmospheres and long-term habitability of orbiting exoplanets. Investigating how this high-energy emission evolves is therefore essential for understanding the evolution of stellar magnetic dynamos and planetary atmospheres and habitability. In this work, we investigate the evolution of X-ray activity and XUV irradiation for a sample of F-M dwarf stars based on Chandra and XMM-Newton observations. We find that F- and G-type stars broadly follow the traditional evolutionary picture of an early saturated (or weakly declining) phase followed by a modest decline, whereas K- and M-type stars exhibit a clear three-phase evolution of a saturated phase, an intermediate phase of rapid decay, and a final modest decline phase. By combining X-ray, ultraviolet, and Ca II H&K bands, we show that coronal emission becomes increasingly dominant toward lower-mass stars. Based on the cumulative XUV emission calculated from our fitted relation, planets around F- and G-type stars experience relatively moderate XUV environments, while those around K- and M-type stars may exceed the empirical cosmic shoreline shortly after reaching the main sequence, though this conclusion depends on the adopted shoreline value.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the evolution of X-ray activity and XUV irradiation for F-M dwarf stars using Chandra and XMM-Newton observations, finding that F/G stars show traditional two-phase evolution while K/M stars exhibit a three-phase evolution, and that K/M-type stars may expose orbiting planets to extreme XUV environments exceeding the cosmic shoreline shortly after reaching the main sequence.
AI.motivation: Stellar X-ray emission is a direct diagnostic of coronal activity and coronal heating, and significantly impacts exoplanet atmospheres and long-term habitability. Understanding how this high-energy emission evolves is essential for constraining stellar magnetic dynamo evolution and planetary atmospheric evolution.
AI.method: The study uses Chandra and XMM-Newton observations of F-M dwarf stars to trace X-ray activity evolution. The authors fit evolutionary relations and combine X-ray, ultraviolet, and Ca II H&K bands to assess coronal emission dominance across spectral types. They then calculate cumulative XUV emission to evaluate the irradiation environments of orbiting planets.
AI.result: F- and G-type stars follow the traditional picture of an early saturated/weakly declining phase followed by a modest decline. K- and M-type stars exhibit a three-phase evolution: saturated, rapid decay, and final modest decline. Coronal emission becomes increasingly dominant toward lower-mass stars. Planets around K- and M-type stars may exceed the empirical cosmic shoreline shortly after reaching the main sequence, while F/G-star planets experience moderate XUV environments.
AI.conclusion: The evolutionary picture of stellar X-ray activity is mass-dependent, with lower-mass stars showing more complex three-phase behavior. The stronger coronal dominance and higher cumulative XUV output around K/M stars suggest these systems may pose challenges to planetary atmosphere retention and habitability, though the finding depends on the adopted cosmic shoreline value.

title: On the Effect of Large Scale Structures and Turbulence on Solar Eruptive Events: The Cross-Scale Challenge for Space Weather
summary: Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) are among the most powerful drivers of space weather, yet their prediction remains elusive. A fundamental obstacle is the problem's multiscale nature: large-scale magnetohydrodynamic models do not resolve the turbulent fluctuations that govern particle transport and magnetic connectivity. We present a new model that combines a MICroscopic diffusion approach of turbulence with MACroscopic EUHFORIA simulations (MICMAC) to address the cross-scale challenge of space weather. By incorporating turbulence properties into such small-scale Monte Carlo simulations, we describe an extreme CME event, tracing both magnetic field lines and 100 MeV protons from the CME-driven shock to 1 AU. We find that turbulence dramatically broadens and distorts the magnetic connection between the CME nose and Earth, producing footpoint distributions that are highly non-Gaussian, anisotropic, and patchy. MICMAC suggests that the distribution's enstrophy (non-Gaussianity) grows as the CME approaches Earth, signaling anomalous diffusive behavior. A simple shear-layer toy model reproduces the observed in-plane anisotropy, suggesting that local current sheet geometry imprints a persistent memory on the turbulent field. Our results demonstrate that cross-scale coupling between the CME's large-scale structure and ambient turbulence must be accounted for in space weather models. We discuss implications for SEP forecasting and interpreting multi-spacecraft observations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents MICMAC, a new model coupling microscopic turbulence diffusion with macroscopic EUHFORIA magnetohydrodynamic simulations to address the multiscale challenge of space weather prediction. Applied to an extreme CME event, the model traces magnetic field lines and 100 MeV protons from the CME-driven shock to 1 AU, revealing that turbulence dramatically broadens, distorts, and fragments the magnetic connection between the CME nose and Earth, producing highly non-Gaussian, anisotropic, and patchy footpoint distributions. The model shows enstrophy (non-Gaussianity) grows as the CME approaches Earth, indicating anomalous diffusion, and a simple shear-layer toy model reproduces the observed in-plane anisotropy.
AI.motivation: CME prediction remains elusive due to the multiscale nature of the problem: large-scale MHD models cannot resolve the turbulent fluctuations that govern particle transport and magnetic connectivity, creating a critical gap in space weather forecasting capability.
AI.method: The MICMAC model couples microscopic turbulence diffusion (via small-scale Monte Carlo simulations incorporating turbulence properties) with macroscopic EUHFORIA MHD simulations, enabling cross-scale modeling that traces both magnetic field lines and 100 MeV protons from the CME-driven shock to 1 AU.
AI.result: Turbulence dramatically broadens and distorts magnetic connectivity between the CME nose and Earth, producing highly non-Gaussian, anisotropic, and patchy footpoint distributions. Enstrophy grows as the CME approaches Earth (anomalous diffusion), and a shear-layer toy model reproduces the observed in-plane anisotropy, indicating local current sheet geometry imprints persistent memory on the turbulent field.
AI.conclusion: Cross-scale coupling between the CME's large-scale structure and ambient turbulence must be accounted for in space weather models, with significant implications for SEP forecasting and interpretation of multi-spacecraft observations.

title: BSN-VII: Photometric Light Curve Study of Three Cool, Large-Amplitude, Low Mass, W-Subtype Contact Binaries
summary: We present a comprehensive photometric study of three W UMa-type contact binary systems, V1104 Her, V1284 Her, and V2822 Ori, based on a combination of ground-based observations and space-based TESS photometry. The light curves were modeled using the BSN application under a contact configuration, with parameters and their uncertainties estimated through the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach. The derived solutions indicate that the target systems are in a shallow-contact configuration. The target systems are classified as W-subtype contact binaries, with the more massive component cooler than its companion. The light curve of V1284 Her shows a pronounced O'Connell effect, which is reproduced by introducing a cool starspot on the primary component. Absolute parameters were estimated using the empirical parameter relationship between orbital period and semi-major axis, yielding component masses in the range $0.48$-$0.86\,M_\odot$ and confirming the low-mass nature of the systems. Orbital period variations were investigated using eclipse timings from the literature, ground-based observations, and TESS data by examining both linear and cyclic models. Statistical model comparison indicates that the cyclic model provides a better description of the eclipse timings for V1104 Her and V1284 Her, whereas the linear model is preferred for V2822 Ori, although the difference between the two models is relatively small.

AI.tldr: A comprehensive photometric study of three W UMa-type contact binaries (V1104 Her, V1284 Her, V2822 Ori) using ground-based and TESS photometry, revealing shallow-contact, W-subtype configurations with a cool starspot on V1284 Her's primary component, low-mass components (0.48–0.86 M☉), and orbital period variation analyses favoring cyclic models for two systems and linear for the third.
AI.motivation: To conduct a detailed photometric analysis of three W UMa-type contact binary systems to determine their physical and orbital parameters, classification, and investigate their orbital period variations, thereby contributing to the understanding of low-mass contact binary evolution and structure.
AI.method: Combined ground-based and space-based TESS photometry were employed. Light curves were modeled using the BSN application under a contact configuration, with parameters and uncertainties derived via the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) approach. The O'Connell effect in V1284 Her was modeled with a cool starspot on the primary component. Absolute parameters were estimated using the empirical orbital period–semi-major axis relationship. Orbital period variations were analyzed using linear and cyclic models fitted to eclipse timings from literature, ground-based data, and TESS, with statistical model comparison via (presumably) information criteria or likelihood ratio tests.
AI.result: All three systems are shallow-contact, W-subtype binaries with the more massive component being cooler. V1284 Her exhibits a pronounced O'Connell effect successfully reproduced by a cool starspot. Component masses range from 0.48 to 0.86 M☉, confirming low-mass nature. The cyclic model better explains eclipse timings for V1104 Her and V1284 Her, while the linear model is preferred for V2822 Ori (though the difference is small).
AI.conclusion: The three systems are confirmed as shallow-contact, W-subtype, low-mass contact binaries. Their orbital period variations suggest cyclic modulations (likely indicative of a third body or magnetic activity cycles) for V1104 Her and V1284 Her, while V2822 Ori shows no strong preference for a cyclic variation. The small model differences highlight the need for continued monitoring of these systems.

title: MEGARA Stellar Spectral Library. Second Release
summary:
We present the second release of the MEGARA spectral library, MEGASTAR, which now includes all spectra collected during ten observing semesters at the Gran Telescopio CANARIAS. This new release supersedes our first release and incorporates a substantial number of additional observations (2000 new spectra), obtained at high spectral resolution, R(FWHM)$\sim$20000, in two wavelength ranges centred on H$α$ (6420 - 6790 A) and on the CaII triplet (8370 - 8885 A).
  The aim of this paper is to introduce MEGASTAR DR2 to the community as its high-resolution spectra can serve as a valuable resource for numerous types of research. In particular, we will use MEGASTAR spectra to construct SSP blocks within the HR-PyPopStar evolutionary synthesis models.
  The stars were observed using the integral field spectroscopy mode of the instrument. We process the data in a uniform way with the MEGARA data reduction pipeline. We estimate the stellar flux by adding the spectra from 37 spaxels, centred on the spaxel with the highest flux in the IFU reconstructed image. This approach guarantees that the effective slit width, and therefore the spectral resolution, are the same for all spectra.
  The second MEGASTAR release consists of 2838 spectra corresponding to 1408 stars, providing a better coverage of the stellar parameter space than the first release. The spectra were acquired with an average continuum S/N of about 215.
  This second release meets the standards of a modern empirical library: it offers reliable calibrations, data free from slit effects, observations of a large number of stars, and provides high spectral resolution to model both individual stellar clusters and entire galaxies observed with MEGARA.

AI.tldr: This paper presents MEGASTAR DR2, the second release of the MEGARA spectral library, containing 2838 high-resolution (R~20000) spectra of 1408 stars collected over ten observing semesters at the Gran Telescopio CANARIAS. The library covers two wavelength ranges (Hα and CaII triplet) and is intended for use in constructing SSP blocks for HR-PyPopStar evolutionary synthesis models.
AI.motivation: To introduce the second release of the MEGASTAR spectral library to the community, as its high-resolution spectra serve as a valuable resource for diverse research, particularly for constructing simple stellar population (SSP) blocks within the HR-PyPopStar evolutionary synthesis models.
AI.method: Stars were observed using the integral field spectroscopy (IFS) mode of the MEGARA instrument at the Gran Telescopio CANARIAS. Data were processed uniformly with the MEGARA data reduction pipeline, and stellar flux was estimated by co-adding spectra from 37 spaxels centered on the brightest spaxel in the IFU reconstructed image, ensuring consistent effective slit width and spectral resolution across all spectra.
AI.result: The second MEGASTAR release comprises 2838 spectra of 1408 stars with improved stellar parameter space coverage compared to the first release. The spectra have an average continuum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 215, with high spectral resolution (R~20000) in two wavelength ranges centered on Hα and the CaII triplet.
AI.conclusion: MEGASTAR DR2 meets modern empirical library standards, offering reliable calibrations, data free of slit effects, a large stellar sample, and high spectral resolution—making it suitable for modeling individual stellar clusters and entire galaxies observed with MEGARA.

title: Origin of small-scale evaporation flows deep in the chromosphere during a solar flare
comment: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters (Issue: Sunrise III Early Science)
summary: Flares are caused by an abrupt release of magnetic energy in the solar atmosphere. Plasma heated to well over 10 MK filling the post-flare corona originates from a rapid heating and ablation of the cooler chromospheric material. This chromospheric evaporation is thought to be facilitated primarily by nonthermal electrons impinging on to the lower atmosphere. Questions on when and where in the chromosphere these upflows originate, however, are not fully resolved. Here we report on unprecedented high-resolution observations of an M-class flare recorded by the Sunrise Ultraviolet Spectropolarimeter and Imager on board the balloon-borne SUNRISE observatory, that reveal highly structured upflows on spatial scales of ~100 km originating deep in the chromosphere. The flows even precede the onset of nonthermal electrons by about 10 minutes and last through the impulsive phase of the flare. Our observations shed new light on the lower atmospheric heating and mass circulation in flares that are challenging to reconcile with the standard solar flare model.

AI.tldr: High-resolution observations of an M-class flare reveal highly structured chromospheric upflows on ~100 km scales that originate deep in the chromosphere and precede nonthermal electron onset by ~10 minutes, challenging the standard solar flare model.
AI.motivation: To resolve open questions about when and where chromospheric evaporation upflows originate during solar flares, which are thought to be driven primarily by nonthermal electrons.
AI.method: Analysis of unprecedented high-resolution observations from the Sunrise Ultraviolet Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUNRISE observatory) of an M-class flare.
AI.result: Revealed highly structured upflows on ~100 km spatial scales originating deep in the chromosphere; these flows precede nonthermal electron onset by ~10 minutes and persist through the impulsive phase.
AI.conclusion: The observations shed new light on lower atmospheric heating and mass circulation in flares that are challenging to reconcile with the standard solar flare model, suggesting chromospheric evaporation dynamics may be more complex than currently understood.

title: Type I Solar Radio Bursts Modulated by Solar Flares
summary: Type I solar radio bursts (noise storms) are persistent meter-wave nonthermal emissions above active regions, with their occurrence and proper?ties closely related to the local magnetic configuration and nonthermal electron acceleration. This study examines a type I noise storm on 24 December 2023 and its relation to flare activity. The noise-storm source was co-spatial with active region AR 3529 and showed frequency-dependent spatial dispersion. The associated M2.9 flare strongly modulated the emission, with the storm intensity decreasing at flare onset, recovering afterward, and shifting to higher frequencies. Based on multiwavelength observations, we suggest that pre-flare small-scale reconnection supplied nonthermal electrons to overlying closed magnetic struc?tures and maintained the storm. During the flare, magnetic reconnection above the active region produced bidirectional plasma ejections and type III bursts with bidirectional frequency drifts; the gradually decreasing starting frequency of these bursts may indicate an upward-moving reconnection site. The resulting magnetic reconfiguration disrupted electron trapping and suppressed the storm, whereas post-flare magnetic recovery allowed the emission to resume. These results show that flares can modulate type I noise storms through magnetic restructuring and provide insight into the generation mechanism of noise storms.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a type I solar radio noise storm observed on 24 December 2023, co-spatial with AR 3529, and shows how an associated M2.9 flare modulated the storm: the storm intensity decreased at flare onset, recovered afterward, and shifted to higher frequencies due to magnetic restructuring above the active region.
AI.motivation: Type I solar radio bursts (noise storms) are persistent meter-wave emissions whose occurrence and properties are linked to local magnetic configurations and nonthermal electron acceleration. The authors aim to understand the relationship between type I noise storms and flare activity, and how magnetic restructuring influences storm generation and suppression.
AI.method: The authors use multiwavelength observations of a type I noise storm on 24 December 2023, examining its spatial co-location with AR 3529, frequency-dependent spatial dispersion, and its temporal evolution relative to the associated M2.9 flare. They analyze the modulation of storm intensity, frequency shifts, bidirectional plasma ejections, type III bursts with bidirectional frequency drifts, and track the changing starting frequency of bursts as evidence of reconnection site movement.
AI.result: The noise-storm source was co-spatial with AR 3529 and exhibited frequency-dependent spatial dispersion. The associated M2.9 flare strongly modulated the emission, with storm intensity decreasing at flare onset, recovering afterward, and shifting to higher frequencies. Pre-flare reconnection supplied nonthermal electrons to overlying closed magnetic structures, while flare reconnection produced bidirectional ejections and type III bursts with bidirectional drifts, with a gradually decreasing starting frequency indicating an upward-moving reconnection site. The magnetic reconfiguration disrupted electron trapping and suppressed the storm, but post-flare recovery allowed emission to resume.
AI.conclusion: Flares can modulate type I noise storms through magnetic restructuring. This work provides insight into the generation mechanism of noise storms, showing that the interplay between reconnection-supplied nonthermal electrons and magnetic topology changes governs the storm's intensity and frequency behavior.

title: Ion-Scale Waves Regulated by Plasma Beta and Cross Helicity: Observational Evidence for the Helicity Barrier in Imbalanced Solar Wind Turbulence
summary: Ion-scale waves are believed to play an important role in heating of the solar corona and wind, though their generation mechanism remains unclear. Based on Parker Solar Probe observations, this Letter investigates the occurrence of ion-scale waves in the near-Sun solar wind with heliocentric distances between 0.1 and 0.2 au. Results show that the occurrence rate of left-handed polarized waves significantly depends on the plasma beta ($β$) and cross helicity ($σ_c$). The occurrence rate rapidly increases with decreasing $β$ and increasing $σ_c$. Overall, the occurrence rate exceeds 45$\%$ when $β<0.2$ and $σ_c > 0.7$ are satisfied. These observations are consistent with the direct predictions of the helicity barrier theory that suggests the generation of ion cyclotron waves via imbalanced magnetized turbulence.

AI.tldr: Using Parker Solar Probe data between 0.1–0.2 au, this Letter shows that left-handed polarized ion-scale waves in the near-Sun solar wind occur more frequently at low plasma beta and high cross helicity, with occurrence rates exceeding 45% when β<0.2 and σc>0.7, consistent with the helicity barrier theory.
AI.motivation: Ion-scale waves are thought to contribute to solar corona and wind heating, but their generation mechanism is not well understood. This study aims to constrain the generation mechanism by investigating wave occurrence as a function of plasma parameters in the near-Sun solar wind.
AI.method: Analysis of Parker Solar Probe observations of ion-scale waves in the near-Sun solar wind at heliocentric distances between 0.1 and 0.2 au, examining occurrence rates of left-handed polarized waves as a function of plasma beta (β) and cross helicity (σc), and comparing with predictions of the helicity barrier theory.
AI.result: The occurrence rate of left-handed polarized ion-scale waves strongly depends on β and σc: it increases rapidly with decreasing β and increasing σc. The occurrence rate exceeds 45% when β<0.2 and σc>0.7 simultaneously.
AI.conclusion: The observed parametric dependence of ion-scale wave occurrence is consistent with the helicity barrier theory, which proposes that ion cyclotron waves are generated via imbalanced magnetized turbulence, providing observational support for this generation mechanism.

title: Intermediate-mass runaway and hypervelocity star candidates in DESI DR1
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 12 Pages, 5 Appendix, 20 figures. Abstract shortened
summary: Runaway stars ejected from the Galactic disc span a range of velocities, with two extreme regimes of particular interest. Hyper-runaway stars reach velocities approaching the local Galactic escape speed while remaining gravitationally bound to the Galaxy, while hypervelocity stars (HVS) have speeds which exceed the escape speed, leaving them formally unbound. Studying both populations places stringent constraints on star cluster formation, supernova explosions in massive binaries, and the shape of the stellar halo. Here we present a spectroscopic search for such extreme-velocity stars using data from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). Because these objects are typically located at distances beyond the range where \textit{gaia} parallaxes are reliable, we derive stellar parameters through a combined analysis of spectroscopy and spectral energy distributions (SEDs). These parameters are then compared with stellar evolutionary tracks to infer distances, which are subsequently used to compute the kinematics of the candidates. We identify a sub-sample of eight stars that appear unbound to the Galaxy, likely of extragalactic origin. These stars exhibit projected rotational velocities exceeding $50$ km s$^{-1}$, consistent with a main-sequence nature. An additional eleven stars are identified as potential HVS candidates under the assumption that they are main-sequence stars. This interpretation is not supported by their rotational velocities, making their unbound status less secure. Finally, $26$ stars show evidence of being main-sequence runaway stars ejected from the Galactic disc. The fastest object in the sample is a metal-poor HVS candidate with a Galactocentric velocity upper-limit of $934 \pm 110$ km s$^{-1}$. The star with the largest measured radial velocity of $513$ km s$^{-1}$ is most likely a slowly pulsating B-type runaway star.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a spectroscopic search for extreme-velocity stars (hyper-runaway stars and hypervelocity stars) using DESI DR1 data. By combining spectroscopy and SEDs to derive stellar parameters and infer distances via evolutionary tracks, the authors identify 8 unbound stars likely of extragalactic origin, 11 potential HVS candidates, and 26 main-sequence runaway stars ejected from the Galactic disc. The fastest candidate has a Galactocentric velocity upper limit of 934 ± 110 km/s.
AI.motivation: Studying runaway stars and hypervelocity stars provides constraints on star cluster formation, supernova explosions in massive binaries, and the shape of the stellar halo. These extreme-velocity populations represent two regimes of interest: hyper-runaway stars (bound but fast) and hypervelocity stars (unbound).
AI.method: The authors use DESI DR1 data for a spectroscopic search. Since these stars are typically at distances beyond reliable Gaia parallax coverage, they derive stellar parameters via combined analysis of spectroscopy and spectral energy distributions (SEDs). These parameters are compared with stellar evolutionary tracks to infer distances, which are then used to compute kinematics of the candidates.
AI.result: Identified 8 stars that appear unbound to the Galaxy and likely of extragalactic origin (projected rotational velocities exceeding 50 km/s, consistent with main-sequence nature); 11 potential HVS candidates whose unbound status is less secure due to rotational velocities not supporting main-sequence interpretation; and 26 main-sequence runaway stars ejected from the Galactic disc. The fastest object is a metal-poor HVS candidate with Galactocentric velocity upper limit of 934 ± 110 km/s, and the largest measured radial velocity star (513 km/s) is likely a slowly pulsating B-type runaway star.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates the power of DESI DR1 data combined with SED analysis for finding extreme-velocity stars beyond the range where Gaia parallaxes are reliable, providing a new sample of unbound/hypervelocity star candidates and runaway stars for further study.

title: Moment-based formulas for the transport coefficients
summary:
The coefficients of the transport equations, describing the propagation features, are particularly important in astrophysics, interplanetary physics, and experimental plasma physics. 
In this paper, the variable-dependent diffusion coefficients are investigated. For the momentum transport equations, we find that the coefficients are related to statistical quantities, some of which are new. In addition, these coefficients take logarithmic forms, which are different from the results derived in previous papers. For isotropic pitch-angle scattering, we also obtain a formula that takes a logarithmic form. For fractional transport equations, the coefficients expressed in terms of the moments are obtained from the governing equations.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates variable-dependent diffusion coefficients in transport equations relevant to astrophysics and plasma physics. The authors find that coefficients in momentum transport equations relate to (partly new) statistical quantities and take logarithmic forms, differing from prior results. They also derive a logarithmic formula for isotropic pitch-angle scattering and express coefficients for fractional transport equations in terms of moments.
AI.motivation: The coefficients of transport equations describing propagation features are particularly important in astrophysics, interplanetary physics, and experimental plasma physics, motivating a deeper investigation of their form and dependence on variables.
AI.method: The authors analyze variable-dependent diffusion coefficients within momentum transport equations, derive their statistical relationships (some new), and obtain formulas for isotropic pitch-angle scattering and fractional transport equations, expressing coefficients in terms of moments derived from the governing equations.
AI.result: The coefficients are found to be related to statistical quantities, some of which are new, and take logarithmic forms—differing from previous derivations. A logarithmic formula is also obtained for isotropic pitch-angle scattering, and fractional transport equation coefficients are expressed via moments.
AI.conclusion: The study provides new expressions for variable-dependent diffusion coefficients in transport equations, including logarithmic forms that deviate from earlier results, and extends the formulation to fractional transport equations.

title: OB stars identified in LAMOST Data Release 10
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables, accepted by ApJS
summary: A large sample of OB stars plays an important role in studying the stellar parameters of massive stars, as well as the formation and evolution of the Milky Way. With the help of the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) Data Release 10 (DR10), we are able to construct a large sample of OB stars with spectroscopic data. In this study, we identify 48,463 spectra of 34,550 OB stars from LAMOST DR10, based on the Hertzsprung-Russell (H-R) diagram constructed with Gaia DR3 data and spectral line indices measured from LAMOST DR10 low-resolution spectra. Among these, 6907 OB stars are newly identified. We use the MKCLASS tool to derive the spectral subtypes of the OB sample. The spatial distribution of 25,287 OB stars and the Toomre diagram of 20,397 OB stars indicate that the majority of these stars are located in the Galactic disk. Based on their peculiar velocities, we identify 1960 runaway star candidates.

AI.tldr: This study identifies 48,463 spectra of 34,550 OB stars from LAMOST DR10 using Gaia DR3-based H-R diagrams and spectral line indices. Among these, 6,907 OB stars are newly identified. Spectral subtypes are derived using the MKCLASS tool, spatial/kinematic analyses reveal most stars reside in the Galactic disk, and 1,960 runaway star candidates are identified based on peculiar velocities.
AI.motivation: A large sample of OB stars is essential for studying massive stellar parameters and the formation and evolution of the Milky Way, motivating the construction of a comprehensive spectroscopic OB star catalog using LAMOST DR10.
AI.method: OB stars are identified by combining the H-R diagram constructed from Gaia DR3 data and spectral line indices measured from LAMOST DR10 low-resolution spectra. The MKCLASS tool is used to derive spectral subtypes, and spatial distributions, Toomre diagrams, and peculiar velocities are analyzed.
AI.result: A total of 48,463 spectra from 34,550 OB stars are identified, including 6,907 newly identified stars. Spatial and Toomre analyses show most OB stars are in the Galactic disk, and 1,960 runaway star candidates are identified from peculiar velocity analysis.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a large, well-characterized OB star sample from LAMOST DR10, enabling further studies of massive stellar properties, Galactic structure, and runaway stellar populations.

title: Systematic and Statistical Properties of Prominence Eruptions on the M-dwarf YZ CMi
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Conference proceedings of Cool Stars 23, Tokyo, Japan
summary: M-dwarfs produce frequent flares, and their associated mass ejections are expected to significantly affect the habitability of close-in exoplanets. Recent spectroscopic observations have revealed several prominence eruptions-indicative of stellar mass ejections-on M-dwarfs through Doppler shifts of the H$α$ line. However, systematic and statistical studies, particularly regarding their association with white-light flares, have been limited due to the lack of intensive and continuous simultaneous photometric and spectroscopic monitoring of the same target star. We conducted one month of continuous spectroscopic observations of the active M-dwarf YZ CMi using the 3.8-m Seimei telescope with an unprecedentedly high time cadence of $\sim$1 min, simultaneously with TESS. We detected four prominence eruptions, among which two events showed rapid, short-duration eruptions with velocities of $\sim$300-500 km s$^{-1}$ and durations of $\sim$5 min. Such short-duration events may have been missed in previous observations due to insufficient time cadence. We further performed a systematic analysis using 35 H$α$ flares on YZ CMi observed simultaneously with TESS. Notably, most prominence eruptions (6 out of 7) were not associated with detectable white-light flares. This result suggests that most observed prominence eruptions on M-dwarfs may have occurred near the stellar limb, where white-light flares are difficult to detect, which may imply a potential observational bias in their detectability due to low contrast with the background emission. These first statistical constraints, together with the discovery of rapid, short-duration prominence eruptions, indicate that previous observations may have underestimated both the frequency and velocities of mass ejections on M-dwarfs due to observational biases and highlight the necessity of reassessing their impact on close-in exoplanets.

AI.tldr: Using one month of continuous high-cadence (~1 min) spectroscopic observations of the M-dwarf YZ CMi with the Seimei telescope simultaneously with TESS, the authors detected four prominence eruptions (two of which were rapid, short-duration events at 300-500 km/s) and conducted a systematic statistical analysis of 35 Hα flares. Most prominence eruptions (6 out of 7) were not associated with detectable white-light flares, suggesting a potential observational bias toward limb events, implying previous studies underestimated the frequency and velocities of M-dwarf mass ejections and their impact on exoplanet habitability.
AI.motivation: M-dwarf flares and associated mass ejections significantly affect the habitability of close-in exoplanets, but systematic statistical studies of prominence eruptions and their association with white-light flares have been limited due to the lack of intensive, continuous simultaneous photometric and spectroscopic monitoring of the same target.
AI.method: One month of continuous spectroscopic observations of YZ CMi using the 3.8-m Seimei telescope at an unprecedentedly high time cadence of ~1 minute, conducted simultaneously with TESS photometry. Prominence eruptions were detected via Doppler shifts of the Hα line, and a systematic analysis of 35 Hα flares was performed with their TESS white-light counterparts.
AI.result: Four prominence eruptions were detected, two of which were rapid, short-duration events with velocities of ~300-500 km/s and durations of ~5 minutes, likely missed by previous lower-cadence observations. Notably, most prominence eruptions (6 out of 7) were not associated with detectable white-light flares, suggesting they occurred near the stellar limb where white-light flares are difficult to detect due to low contrast.
AI.conclusion: The first statistical constraints on M-dwarf prominence eruptions reveal observational biases that may have led previous studies to underestimate both the frequency and velocities of stellar mass ejections. This highlights the necessity of reassessing the impact of these events on close-in exoplanet habitability.

title: Phosphorus abundances and multi-element co-enrichment in nearby FGK stars
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The distribution of bio-essential elements is key to assessing the chemical fertility of galactic environments. We analyse phosphorus abundances for 233 nearby FGK stars from the Hypatia Catalog, separating thin- and thick-disk populations. We study [P/Fe] as a function of [Fe/H] and other elemental abundances using non-parametric tests and bootstrap resampling, and we examine residual correlations at fixed [Fe/H] together with molar ratios involving P. We find a [P/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend broadly similar to that of alpha elements, supporting a dominant origin in core-collapse supernovae, while deviations point to additional nucleosynthetic channels. Phosphorus shows strong positive correlations with several CHNOPS, alpha, and Fe-peak elements, especially in the thin disk. These co-enrichment patterns remain significant at fixed [Fe/H], indicating that they are not a trivial consequence of global metallicity. Thin-disk stars are also more enriched than thick-disk stars in many elements. The solar P/Mg and P/Si ratios are representative of the local stellar population, whereas solar P/O is relatively elevated. Overall, phosphorus emerges as a tracer of genuine multi-element co-enrichment and of the chemical fertility of the solar neighbourhood.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes phosphorus abundances in 233 nearby FGK stars from the Hypatia Catalog, separating thin- and thick-disk populations to study [P/Fe] trends as functions of [Fe/H] and other elements. The [P/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend resembles alpha elements, supporting a dominant core-collapse supernova origin, while strong co-enrichment with CHNOPS, alpha, and Fe-peak elements persists even at fixed [Fe/H]. Thin-disk stars are more enriched in many elements than thick-disk stars. Solar P/Mg and P/Si ratios are representative of the local stellar population, while solar P/O is elevated.
AI.motivation: To assess the chemical fertility of galactic environments by understanding the distribution and nucleosynthetic origins of phosphorus, a bio-essential element, across different stellar populations in the solar neighbourhood.
AI.method: Use of 233 nearby FGK stars from the Hypatia Catalog, separating thin- and thick-disk populations. Analysis of [P/Fe] as a function of [Fe/H] and other elemental abundances using non-parametric statistical tests and bootstrap resampling, examination of residual correlations at fixed [Fe/H], and evaluation of molar ratios involving P.
AI.result: The [P/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend is broadly similar to alpha elements, indicating a dominant core-collapse supernova origin with deviations pointing to additional nucleosynthetic channels. Phosphorus shows strong positive correlations with CHNOPS, alpha, and Fe-peak elements, especially in the thin disk, and these co-enrichment patterns remain significant at fixed [Fe/H]. Thin-disk stars are more enriched than thick-disk stars in many elements. Solar P/Mg and P/Si ratios match the local stellar population, whereas solar P/O is relatively high.
AI.conclusion: Phosphorus serves as a tracer of genuine multi-element co-enrichment and of the chemical fertility of the solar neighbourhood, with its abundance patterns in the thin/thick disks providing insight into nucleosynthetic origins beyond core-collapse supernovae.

title: Equilibrium \(\mathrm{H}_2^+/\mathrm{H}^-\) Abundance Ratios in MARCS Atmosphere Models
summary: We investigate the equilibrium abundance ratio of the molecular hydrogen ion \(\mathrm{H}_2^+\) and the negative hydrogen ion \(\mathrm{H}^-\) in stellar atmospheres using compact Saha-type equilibrium expressions and layer-by-layer partial pressures from MARCS model atmospheres. The analysis distinguishes the temperature-dependent coefficient ratio \(K_{\mathrm{H}_2^+}(T)/K_{\mathrm{H}^-}(T)\) from the full abundance ratio, which also depends on the local ionisation factor \(N_{\mathrm{H}^+}/N_e\). The internal partition function \(Z_{\mathrm{H}_2^+}(T)\) is included in the \(\mathrm{H}_2^+\) equilibrium coefficient. We processed \(51{,}994\) MARCS models, corresponding to \(2{,}911{,}664\) atmospheric layers, and computed \(N(\mathrm{H}_2^+)/N(\mathrm{H}^-)\) directly from the tabulated equilibrium partial pressures, constructing the first systematic map of this ratio across the MARCS grid. \(\mathrm{H}_2^+\) exceeds \(\mathrm{H}^-\) in \(827{,}350\) layers, corresponding to \(F=0.284\), or \(28.4\%\) of all analysed layers. Although \(\mathrm{H}^-\) remains dominant in the global logarithmic mean, with \(\langle \log_{10}[N(\mathrm{H}_2^+)/N(\mathrm{H}^-)] \rangle=-4.229\), \(\mathrm{H}_2^+\) becomes comparable to or more abundant than \(\mathrm{H}^-\) in a substantial subset of layers. Its relative significance increases toward higher \(T_{\mathrm{eff}}\), lower \([\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]\), and deeper layers. The balance is therefore controlled by the combined local thermodynamic and ionisation structure, not by temperature alone. These ratios are equilibrium abundance diagnostics and do not imply opacity dominance; assessing opacity requires wavelength-dependent cross-sections and radiative-transfer calculations.

AI.tldr: The paper maps the equilibrium abundance ratio of H2+ and H- ions across 51,994 MARCS stellar atmosphere models (2.9 million layers), finding H2+ exceeds H- in 28.4% of layers despite H- dominating the global mean (log ratio = -4.229). The ratio depends on both temperature and the local ionisation factor NH+/Ne, with H2+ significance increasing toward higher Teff, lower metallicity, and deeper layers.
AI.motivation: To construct the first systematic map of the H2+/H- equilibrium abundance ratio across the full MARCS model grid, clarifying under what stellar atmospheric conditions H2+ can become comparable to or exceed the well-known H- ion, and distinguishing temperature effects from ionisation-structure effects.
AI.method: Used compact Saha-type equilibrium expressions with the internal partition function of H2+ included, combined layer-by-layer partial pressures from 51,994 MARCS model atmospheres (2,911,664 layers). Separated the temperature-dependent coefficient ratio KH2+(T)/KH-(T) from the full abundance ratio that also involves the local ionisation factor NH+/Ne.
AI.result: H2+ exceeds H- in 827,350 layers (28.4% of all layers). The global logarithmic mean of the ratio is -4.229 (H- dominant overall), but H2+ becomes comparable or more abundant in a substantial subset. The significance of H2+ increases with higher effective temperature, lower [Fe/H], and deeper atmospheric layers.
AI.conclusion: The H2+/H- balance is governed by the combined local thermodynamic and ionisation structure rather than temperature alone. The computed ratios serve as equilibrium abundance diagnostics and do not imply opacity dominance; assessing actual opacity requires wavelength-dependent cross-sections and full radiative-transfer calculations.

title: Joint Observations of PTPS Targets (JOTA). Combined spectroscopic and photometric analysis of 16 SB1 systems
summary: Context. The Pennsylvania-Toruń Planet Search, which operates on a sample of $\sim$1000 northern-hemisphere stars, has been underway since 2004. Stars with radial velocity (RV) amplitudes exceeding 2 km s$^{-1}$ represent a backup subprogram sample dedicated to monitoring binary stars with multiple instruments. Aims. We used almost 21 years of combined RV measurements to search for Doppler signals consistent with stellar or brown dwarf companions and to produce a catalog of both known and previously unpublished binary stars in our planet-search sample. Methods. We analyzed the combined RV measurements, searching for stellar companions and obtaining orbital solutions for both known and new binary systems. We also searched for periods in available long-term photometric monitoring data from All Sky Automated Survey (ASAS), and applied Gaia astrometric data whenever available. Results. We report the results of long-term RV monitoring of 16 systems: new detections of low-mass companions to 11 stars and updated orbital elements based on combined sets of our new and literature data for five systems. For two objects (TYC 3318-00789-1 and TYC 3318-01538-1), we find evidence of activity or the influence of another unseen companion, possibly due to line-profile variations or unresolved spectral contamination. We present true masses for three systems in our sample: TYC 1931-1040-1, TYC 3451- 1449-1, and TYC 3667-1636-1. We obtained these masses using Gaia DR3 non-single star data.

AI.tldr: Using ~21 years of combined radial velocity measurements from the Pennsylvania-Toruń Planet Search, the authors monitored 16 binary systems, discovering low-mass stellar/brown dwarf companions to 11 stars, updating orbital elements for 5 known systems, and deriving true masses for 3 systems using Gaia DR3 astrometric data.
AI.motivation: To search for Doppler signals consistent with stellar or brown dwarf companions and produce a catalog of both known and previously unpublished binary stars within the ~1000-star sample of the Pennsylvania-Toruń Planet Search.
AI.method: Combined and analyzed nearly 21 years of RV measurements to detect stellar companions and derive orbital solutions. Searched for periods in long-term ASAS photometric monitoring and incorporated Gaia DR3 astrometric data (non-single star solutions) when available.
AI.result: New low-mass companions detected around 11 stars; updated orbital elements for 5 known systems; two objects (TYC 3318-00789-1 and TYC 3318-01538-1) show activity or unseen companion influence; true masses obtained for three systems (TYC 1931-1040-1, TYC 3451-1449-1, TYC 3667-1636-1) using Gaia DR3 data.
AI.conclusion: The long-term monitoring program successfully characterizes binary and substellar companions in the planet-search sample, combining RV, photometric, and astrometric data to derive orbital solutions and in some cases true dynamical masses.

title: Interferometric Survey of Stellar Parameters: Towards homogeneous FGK stars parameters and surface-brightness color relation in the context of PLATO space mission
summary: The estimation of stellar angular diameters can be performed from the surface brightness - color relation (SBCR) and photometry. The SBCR have been considered by the PLATO space mission as an independent empirical alternative for estimating stellar radii of FGK stars. In this context, we have implemented an homogeneous approach not only for calibrating the SBCR for FGK-IV/V stars but, also for determining their fundamental parameters in order to place the stars reliably on the HR diagram and to study their impact on the SBCR. We have performed interferometric observations of 18 quiescent FGK-IV/V stars in the Gaia color range of $3.088 \leq G \leq 5.498$. For the first time, we used 3 different interferometers operating in the $R$, $H$ , and $K$ bands to measure polychromatic limb-darkened angular diameters (LDAD). In parallel, by using public domain spectra we have estimated the stellar parameters ($T_{eff}$, $log g$ and Z) by using the open python tool iSpec. We achieved an average accuracy of 2.3% for the LDAD based on polychromatic observations. However, we have observed that our SBCR does not follow the calibration of the relation between surface brightness and color in Gaia found in the literature. Furthermore, we found that $log g$ and $Z$ have no impact on the SBC relation; given the characteristics of our sample of quiescent stars, it constitutes an ideal set of targets for conducting a new SBCR calibration within the framework of the PLATO space mission. In this context, we reported a SBCR calibration with $σ_{RMS} = $ 0.012, 0.009, 0.009 in the $G, G_{BP}$ and $G_{RP}$ Gaia bands, respectively. This article is part of a series of papers reporting the first results obtained using a polychromatic approach to measure LDAD, employing a fully homogeneous methodology for both determining the fundamental parameters of stars and measuring the LDAD, $θ_{LD}$.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a homogeneous approach to calibrate the surface brightness-color relation (SBCR) for FGK-IV/V stars, combining interferometric limb-darkened angular diameter measurements from three different instruments (R, H, K bands) with stellar parameter estimation via the iSpec tool. The authors achieve 2.3% accuracy on angular diameters, find that log g and metallicity do not affect the SBC relation, and provide a new SBCR calibration with σ_RMS values of 0.012, 0.009, and 0.009 in the G, GBP, and GRP Gaia bands respectively, relevant for the PLATO space mission.
AI.motivation: To provide an independent empirical alternative for estimating stellar radii of FGK stars for the PLATO space mission by calibrating the surface brightness-color relation using a fully homogeneous methodology, including both stellar fundamental parameter determination and polychromatic interferometric angular diameter measurements.
AI.method: The authors used three different interferometers operating in R, H, and K bands to measure polychromatic limb-darkened angular diameters (LDAD) of 18 quiescent FGK-IV/V stars in the Gaia color range 3.088 ≤ G ≤ 5.498. In parallel, they estimated stellar parameters (Teff, log g, Z) using the open Python tool iSpec on public domain spectra. The SBCR was then calibrated against Gaia photometry.
AI.result: The LDAD achieved an average accuracy of 2.3% based on polychromatic observations. The SBCR calibration deviates from the literature calibration. No impact of log g or Z on the SBC relation was found. The reported SBCR calibration yields σ_RMS = 0.012, 0.009, 0.009 in the G, GBP, and GRP Gaia bands, respectively.
AI.conclusion: The quiescent FGK-IV/V sample provides an ideal set of targets for a new SBCR calibration within the PLATO space mission framework. This work is part of a series reporting first results using a polychromatic approach to measure LDAD with a fully homogeneous methodology for both fundamental parameter determination and angular diameter measurement.

title: Astrometric modeling of unresolved variable binary systems. II. Application to Gaia epoch astrometry of nearby pulsating and convective red giants
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures, accepted for publication by Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: (Abbreviated) The interpretation of high-precision astrometry for intrinsically variable stars remains challenging, particularly for unresolved binary systems containing asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars. In such systems, large-amplitude pulsations and evolving convective surface structures induce time-dependent photocentre displacements that perturb the observed orbital motion. At the same time, Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry offers the prospect of deriving accurate orbital solutions and parallaxes for nearby unresolved AGB binaries. Building upon the variability-induced mover (VIM) framework, we extend the astrometric model for unresolved evolved binaries by combining Keplerian photocentre motion, pulsation-induced flux-dependent photocentre shifts, and convection-induced photocentre motion. In the forward simulations, convection is represented either by stochastic photocentre displacements drawn from an exponential correlation function or by photocentre time series extracted from 3D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. We then test a retrieval framework that fits the orbital and VIM signal while incorporating a red-noise covariance matrix to account for correlated astrometric residuals produced by convection. We show that Gaia epoch astrometry can recover reliable orbital and astrometric parameters for unresolved AGB binaries despite strong pulsation- and convection-induced photocentre variability. Pulsation-induced variability produces a coherent VIM signal that can be modeled jointly with the Keplerian photocentre orbit, while convection-induced photocentre motion behaves primarily as temporally correlated astrometric noise. Retrievals that ignore this correlated component lead to biased proper motions and parallaxes, whereas the inclusion of a physically motivated red-noise covariance model enables accurate recovery of the underlying orbital solution and astrometric parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the variability-induced mover (VIM) framework to model astrometric observations of unresolved AGB binary stars, combining Keplerian orbital motion, pulsation-induced photocentre shifts, and convection-induced photocentre noise. Using forward simulations (including stochastic and 3D RHD-derived convection models) and retrieval tests with red-noise covariance, it demonstrates that Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry can recover accurate orbital parameters, parallaxes, and proper motions for unresolved AGB binaries despite strong intrinsic variability.
AI.motivation: Accurate astrometric interpretation for unresolved AGB binaries is difficult because large-amplitude pulsations and evolving surface convection perturb photocentre positions, obscuring the orbital signal in high-precision astrometric data such as Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry.
AI.method: The authors extend the variability-induced mover (VIM) framework by jointly modeling Keplerian photocentre motion, pulsation-induced flux-dependent photocentre shifts, and convection-induced photocentre motion. Forward simulations use either stochastic photocentre displacements with an exponential correlation function or time series from 3D radiation-hydrodynamic simulations. A retrieval framework fits the orbital and VIM signals with a red-noise covariance matrix to account for correlated convection-induced astrometric residuals.
AI.result: Gaia epoch astrometry can reliably recover orbital and astrometric parameters for unresolved AGB binaries despite strong pulsation- and convection-induced variability. Pulsation-induced variability produces a coherent VIM signal that is modeled jointly with the Keplerian orbit, while convection acts as temporally correlated astrometric noise. Ignoring this correlated component biases proper motions and parallaxes; including a physically motivated red-noise covariance model restores accurate recovery.
AI.conclusion: A unified modeling approach incorporating both coherent VIM signals and correlated convection noise is essential for unbiased astrometric parameter recovery of unresolved evolved binaries, and the proposed framework is viable for exploiting Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry for such systems.

title: The umbrella effect: Magnetic canopy topology modulates spatially averaged chromospheric three-minute power
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Three-minute ($\sim$5 mHz) oscillations are a prominent signature of wave propagation in the solar chromosphere, but their measured power can vary substantially between full-disc observations and small, high-resolution fields of view. We investigate whether chromospheric magnetic canopy topology, particularly its lateral continuity and areal filling, modulates field-of-view-averaged three-minute power. We analyse H$α$ and Ca II 8542 Å spectral imaging from the Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope, comparing canopy-poor quiet-Sun scenes with canopy-dominated active-region environments, complemented by radiative-MHD Bifrost simulations of canopy-poor and canopy-rich atmospheres. We compute field-of-view-averaged power spectra from fixed-wavelength intensities and bisector-derived velocities in the observations, and from synthetic intensities, velocities, and temperature proxies in the simulations. We also quantify the relation between integrated 3-5 mHz excess power and canopy filling factor, using HMI-based magnetic-field extrapolations for the observations. In both observations and simulations, canopy-poor scenes show clear 3-5 mHz power enhancements, whereas canopy-dominated scenes show strongly reduced measured power. The trend is present in H$α$ and Ca II 8542 Å intensities and is supported by complementary velocity and temperature proxies. Integrated 3-5 mHz excess power decreases with increasing canopy filling factor. We conclude that chromospheric field-of-view-averaged three-minute power is a topology-weighted observable: dense, laterally continuous magnetic canopies can strongly reduce the measured large-scale three-minute signature without requiring the absence of local wave activity. This provides a practical criterion for interpreting chromospheric oscillation power as a proxy for atmospheric wave energy in the Sun and in magnetised cool-star atmospheres.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how chromospheric magnetic canopy topology modulates field-of-view-averaged three-minute (~5 mHz) oscillation power. Using SST observations (Hα and Ca II 8542 Å) and Bifrost radiative-MHD simulations, the authors show that canopy-poor scenes exhibit clear 3-5 mHz power enhancements while canopy-dominated scenes show strongly reduced measured power, with integrated excess power decreasing with increasing canopy filling factor. They conclude that three-minute power is a topology-weighted observable, not a direct measure of wave activity.
AI.motivation: Three-minute oscillations in the solar chromosphere show substantial power variations between full-disc observations and small high-resolution fields of view, and the cause of this discrepancy is unclear. The authors hypothesize that chromospheric magnetic canopy topology—specifically lateral continuity and areal filling—modulates measured oscillation power, which is important for correctly interpreting chromospheric power as a proxy for atmospheric wave energy in the Sun and cool stars.
AI.method: The study combines Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope (SST) Hα and Ca II 8542 Å spectral imaging, comparing canopy-poor quiet-Sun scenes against canopy-dominated active-region environments. This is complemented by Bifrost radiative-MHD simulations of canopy-poor and canopy-rich atmospheres. Field-of-view-averaged power spectra are computed from fixed-wavelength intensities and bisector-derived velocities in observations, and from synthetic intensities, velocities, and temperature proxies in simulations. Canopy filling factor is quantified via HMI-based magnetic-field extrapolations, and the relation between integrated 3-5 mHz excess power and filling factor is established.
AI.result: Both observations and simulations show that canopy-poor scenes display clear 3-5 mHz power enhancements, whereas canopy-dominated scenes show strongly reduced measured power. This trend is consistent across Hα and Ca II 8542 Å intensities and is corroborated by velocity and temperature proxies. Integrated 3-5 mHz excess power decreases with increasing canopy filling factor.
AI.conclusion: Chromospheric field-of-view-averaged three-minute power is a topology-weighted observable: dense, laterally continuous magnetic canopies can strongly suppress the measured large-scale three-minute signature even when local wave activity persists. This provides a practical criterion for interpreting chromospheric oscillation power as a proxy for atmospheric wave energy in the Sun and magnetised cool stars.

title: Study of Butterfly-Shaped Coronal Hole Evolution Across the Solar Disk
summary: We studied the evolution of a butterfly-shaped coronal hole (CH) observed from 2025 September 8 to 14 using SDO/AIA 193~Å images and SDO/HMI line-of-sight magnetograms. The CH boundary was identified using a fixed 100~DN intensity threshold, and its area, mean EUV intensity, and total unsigned magnetic flux were tracked across the solar disk. As the CH approached the central meridian, its area increased from approximately $7.70\times10^{16}$ to $1.63\times10^{17}$~m$^{2}$ and its unsigned magnetic flux from $8.68\times10^{21}$ to $1.91\times10^{22}$~Mx, while the mean 193~Å intensity decreased from about 61 to 45~DN. The area and unsigned flux showed similar temporal trends, whereas the intensity varied oppositely. Near central-meridian passage, these quantities remained relatively stable for several days. A high-speed solar-wind stream was detected at 1~AU about 2--4 days later, reaching 600--750~km~s$^{-1}$, consistent with the CH being its likely solar source. These results link the morphological, radiative, and magnetic evolution of the CH with the subsequent high-speed solar-wind stream.

AI.tldr: This paper tracks the evolution of a butterfly-shaped coronal hole (CH) over a week using SDO/AIA 193 Å images and HMI magnetograms, finding that its area and unsigned magnetic flux increased roughly in tandem while its mean EUV intensity decreased, and a high-speed solar-wind stream arrived at 1 AU 2–4 days later, linking CH evolution to the solar wind.
AI.motivation: To understand how coronal holes' morphological, radiative, and magnetic properties evolve as they traverse the solar disk, and to connect this evolution to the generation of high-speed solar-wind streams observed at 1 AU.
AI.method: CH boundary identified via a fixed 100 DN intensity threshold in SDO/AIA 193 Å images; tracked area, mean EUV intensity, and total unsigned magnetic flux (from SDO/HMI line-of-sight magnetograms) across the solar disk from September 8–14, 2025; compared these trends with in-situ solar-wind speed measurements at 1 AU.
AI.result: Area increased from ~7.70×10^16 to 1.63×10^17 m^2, unsigned magnetic flux from ~8.68×10^21 to 1.91×10^22 Mx, while mean 193 Å intensity decreased from ~61 to 45 DN. Area and flux followed similar trends; intensity varied oppositely. Quantities were stable near central-meridian passage. A high-speed stream at 1 AU arrived 2–4 days later with speeds of 600–750 km/s.
AI.conclusion: The CH's area and magnetic flux expansions and its radiative dimming were consistent with the timing and speed of the subsequent high-speed solar-wind stream, supporting the CH as its solar source and linking CH evolution to the heliospheric wind.

title: Extremes of solar spectral irradiance in the SORCE/XPS record
summary: Extreme and rare changes in space mission solar irradiance records are scientifically relevant but difficult to quantify because these records are finite, instrument dependent, and affected by observational gaps and time varying measurement quality. We evaluated extreme daily logarithmic changes in the band integrated 0.1-7.0 nm irradiance measured by photodiode 7 of the Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment/X-Ray Photometer System (SORCE/XPS) from 2005 to 2019. After constructing a regular daily series by linear interpolation, we analyzed daily logarithmic changes in irradiance and fitted stationary Generalized Extreme Value models to 60 day block maxima and transformed 15 day block minima. Block lengths were selected using Ljung-Box diagnostics and sample autocorrelation functions. Maximum likelihood estimation was used as the primary inferential method, with probability weighted moments as a sensitivity check. The maximum likelihood GEV shape estimates were 0.1661 for maxima and 0.2928 for transformed minima, with closely aligned estimates under the two fitting methods. These positive point estimates are compatible with Fréchet type tails under the selected block constructions. Annualized return levels provide interpretable summaries of extreme relative increases and reductions, but estimates for long return periods remain strongly dependent on extrapolation beyond the 15 year record. Reported measurement precision and absolute uncertainty were used to qualify the interpretation of the fitted tails and were not propagated through the likelihood. By combining EVT based tail modeling with explicit consideration of measurement precision, absolute uncertainty, interpolation, and mission data gaps, the analysis provides an uncertainty aware astrostatistical baseline for extreme value inference from processed solar mission records.

AI.tldr: This paper applies stationary Generalized Extreme Value (GEV) models to daily logarithmic changes in SORCE/XPS solar irradiance (0.1-7.0 nm) from 2005-2019, finding positive shape parameters (0.1661 for maxima, 0.2928 for transformed minima) consistent with Fréchet-type tails, providing an uncertainty-aware astrostatistical baseline for extreme value inference from processed solar mission records.
AI.motivation: Extreme and rare changes in space mission solar irradiance records are scientifically relevant but difficult to quantify because such records are finite, instrument dependent, affected by observational gaps, and have time-varying measurement quality.
AI.method: The analysis constructs a regular daily series via linear interpolation, analyzes daily logarithmic irradiance changes, and fits stationary GEV models to 60-day block maxima and transformed 15-day block minima. Block lengths were selected using Ljung-Box diagnostics and sample autocorrelation functions. Maximum likelihood estimation was primary, with probability weighted moments as sensitivity check. Measurement precision and absolute uncertainty were used to qualify interpretations but not propagated through the likelihood.
AI.result: Maximum likelihood GEV shape estimates were 0.1661 for maxima and 0.2928 for transformed minima, with closely aligned estimates under both fitting methods. These positive point estimates are compatible with Fréchet-type tails. Annualized return levels provide interpretable summaries, though long return period estimates remain strongly dependent on extrapolation beyond the 15-year record.
AI.conclusion: By combining EVT-based tail modeling with explicit consideration of measurement precision, absolute uncertainty, interpolation, and mission data gaps, the analysis provides an uncertainty-aware astrostatistical baseline for extreme value inference from processed solar mission records.

title: From spectroscopic abundances to evolutionary [$α$/Fe] in stellar models
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Large-scale, high-resolution spectroscopic surveys map detailed chemical abundance patterns for millions of stars. However, libraries of stellar evolution models and isochrones still rely on a simplified description of chemical abundances, generally assuming either solar-scaled compositions or a constant enrichment for all $α$-elements. Moreover, the definition of $α$-enrichment is survey-dependent and is not necessarily the most relevant quantity for stellar structure and evolution. In the era of precision stellar astrophysics, stellar models need to better account for the wealth of chemical information provided by spectroscopic surveys. We develop a perturbative method to compute stellar evolution tracks for stars with arbitrary patterns of $α$-elements. We quantify the response of stellar evolutionary tracks to variations of individual $α$-elements through polynomial expansions, which can be linearly combined to produce synthetic tracks for a given abundance pattern. We also introduce the evolutionary $α$-enhancement, [$α$/Fe]$_{\rm ev}$, a constant enhancement for all $α$-elements that reproduces the impact of an observed abundance pattern on stellar models. We validate both methods using stars with detailed APOGEE abundances and quantify the differences between spectroscopic [$α$/Fe] and [$α$/Fe]$_{\rm ev}$ for different surveys. We identify a minimal set of chemical elements required for accurate stellar models and present ALCHEMY, a simple and fast tool to compute [$α$/Fe]$_{\rm ev}$ for general $α$-element abundance patterns.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a perturbative method for computing stellar evolution tracks with arbitrary α-element abundance patterns, introduces the concept of evolutionary α-enhancement [α/Fe]_ev, and presents ALCHEMY, a fast tool to compute this quantity for general abundance patterns observed in large spectroscopic surveys.
AI.motivation: Large-scale spectroscopic surveys provide detailed chemical abundance data for millions of stars, but stellar evolution model libraries still rely on simplified chemical descriptions (solar-scaled or uniform α-enhancement). The definition of α-enrichment is survey-dependent and may not reflect what actually matters for stellar structure and evolution, creating a gap between observational data and theoretical models in the era of precision stellar astrophysics.

They quantify how stellar tracks respond to variations of individual α-elements using polynomial expansions that can be linearly combined to generate synthetic tracks for any given abundance pattern. They also introduce the evolutionary α-enhancement [α/Fe]_ev, which represents a constant α-enhancement that reproduces the impact of a full observed abundance pattern on stellar models, and validate it using APOGEE data.

AI.conclusion: The perturbative method and the evolutionary α-enhancement concept bridge the gap between detailed spectroscopic observations and stellar evolution modeling, enabling more accurate stellar models that properly account for full chemical abundance patterns provided by large surveys.

title: Accretion Rates and Thermohaline Convection in Polluted White Dwarfs
comment: Submitted to AAS Journals, comments welcome!
summary: Polluted white dwarfs provide a unique window into the composition of exoplanetary material, but interpreting their surface abundances requires a quantitative understanding of the mixing processes in their envelopes. Accretion of metal-rich debris onto hydrogen-rich white dwarfs drives thermohaline (fingering) convection in the underlying radiative zone. Previous studies have modeled this as enhanced diffusive transport, often inferring mass accretion rates, $\dot{M}_{\rm acc}$, that exceed constraints from X-ray observations. Here we develop a time-dependent model that treats thermohaline mixing as a propagating front whose evolution is coupled self-consistently to the surface abundance of heavy elements. We perform hydrodynamical simulations which demonstrate that thermohaline mixing drives the composition gradient towards marginal stability. Using this condition, we derive analytic solutions in shallow and deep stratification regimes, finding that the mixed layer depth, $h$, and surface abundance, $X_{\rm surf}$, both scale as $t^{1/2}$ at early times, transitioning to $h \propto t^{4/27}$ and $X_{\rm surf} \propto t^{10/27}$ at later times. The mixed layer reaches depths of only $\sim 100$ km over $10^5$ yr and, without gravitational settling, never reaches a steady state. Including settling leads to an equilibrium surface abundance scaling as $X_{\rm surf, eq} \propto \dot{M}_{\rm acc}^{30/43}$. Applied to G 29--38, the model matches the observed heavy-element abundance for $\dot{M}_{\rm acc} \sim 2\times 10^9$--$4\times 10^{9}~\mathrm{g~s^{-1}}$, in better agreement with X-ray constraints than prior estimates incorporating thermohaline mixing. We also present a general scaling relation for inferring accretion rates directly from observed surface abundances and stellar properties, giving a practical prescription for other polluted white dwarfs.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a time-dependent model of thermohaline (fingering) convection in polluted white dwarfs, treating it as a propagating front coupled to surface heavy-element abundances. Hydrodynamical simulations show the composition gradient approaches marginal stability, from which analytic scaling laws are derived for mixed-layer depth and surface abundance. Applied to G 29–38, the model yields accretion rates (2–4 × 10^9 g s⁻¹) consistent with X-ray constraints, and provides a general prescription for inferring accretion rates in other polluted white dwarfs.
AI.motivation: Previous studies modeled thermohaline mixing in accreted white dwarfs as enhanced diffusive transport, leading to inferred mass accretion rates that exceed X-ray observational constraints. A time-dependent, self-consistent treatment of thermohaline mixing as a propagating front is needed to reconcile abundance interpretations with independent observational limits.
AI.method: The authors develop a time-dependent model coupling thermohaline mixing front propagation to surface heavy-element abundances. They perform hydrodynamical simulations showing the composition gradient is driven toward marginal stability, and use this condition to derive analytic solutions in shallow and deep stratification regimes. They also incorporate gravitational settling to obtain equilibrium abundance scalings.
